Upper bound 273560: the struct instance is the global fetchState@0x14D2B0A20 (dynamic_initializer_for_bdUserStorageStaticPools@0x140342a80 passes &fetchState to InitSlots, and its 24-element arrays sit at fetchState+0x188, +0x1988, +0x30C8, +0x3548, +0x4C88, +0x425B8, all matching the IDA offsets); the next named global is controllerStatData@0x14D2F36B8 = fetchState+273560, and no xref lands in the 0x14D2F3699..0x14D2F36B8 gap. Game-test 273536 (0x42C80) lies inside these bounds but nothing in Replay proves it. No Replay whole-object clear or copy of fetchState was found (the only xrefs to its base are the initializer's lea and the InitSlots call).

structs.notes: Every confirmed offset in IDA's current layout matches Replay (IDA's 392, 6536, 12488, 13640, 19592, 271496, 271592, 271784, 271800, 273528 are right); the builder layout (+24 shift from 392 onward, prior-only) is refuted by these Replay offsets. The struct instance is the global fetchState@0x14D2B0A20 (typed by InitSlots's argument). The LiveStorage MOTD globals named s_liveStorageMotdText@0x14D2B0A28 and s_motdByteCount@0x14D2B0B48 lie inside fetchState (at +8 and +296) and are used as m_fileName[0] and m_fileSize[0]; the two names cannot both be right, see renames. dwMultiFileTask::SetContext is the only Replay function named for this class; it stores its argument at +271784 (m_context), so it is an m_context setter, not a size source. No deleting destructor, allocation, or array-stride use of this struct was found in Replay.
